data.title: Uniform Advantage Expands Retail Presence with Acquisition of 16 Former Scrubs & Beyond Locations
data.description:
New locations across 11 states will provide healthcare professionals with continued access to scrubs, uniforms, and in-store shopping. 

FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla., Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Uniform Advantage has finalized the acquisition of 16 former Scrubs and Beyond retail locations, marking a significant expansion of its brick-and-mortar presence acr Uniform Advantage, a leading retailer of medical uniforms and accessories, has acquired 16 former Scrubs & Beyond retail locations, expanding its presence across the country and bringing the brand to eight new states.

The acquisition follows the closure of more than 115 Scrubs & Beyond stores by former parent company Kindthread. With many healthcare professionals losing access to their neighborhood uniform stores, Uniform Advantage saw an opportunity to keep these locations open and continue serving the communities that depend on them.

"For years, healthcare professionals have been asking us to open stores in their area, so when we learned that former Scrubs and Beyond locations were available, we saw a wonderful opportunity to make that happen in select markets. These stores let us bring our exclusive brands and other brands directly to local communities, where people can touch, feel, try on and see our garments in person and find the fit that works for them. We're thrilled to welcome these communities to Uniform Advantage," said Susan Masimore, CEO of Uniform Advantage.

The 16 locations bring Uniform Advantage into eight new states: Texas, Kansas, Washington, Arizona, Michigan, Missouri, Nebraska, and New Mexico, while expanding its existing presence in California, Florida, and Georgia.

As part of the transition, Uniform Advantage made every effort to retain existing store employees, recognizing the relationships they have built with local healthcare professionals over the years. While not every team member will remain, the company has worked to preserve as much of that experience and local knowledge as possible.

More Brands, More Styles, More Choices 
The stores are now transitioning to the Uniform Advantage brand, with new merchandise arriving regularly. Customers will begin seeing a broader selection of scrubs, styles, colors, and sizes as the company builds out each location's assortment through March 2027. During the transition, product selection may vary by location.

Shoppers can look forward to Uniform Advantage's exclusive brands, including Butter-Soft, Easy STRETCH, and Hypothesis, alongside popular national brands such as Cherokee, Healing Hands, Med Couture, Grey's Anatomy, and Skechers.

For Uniform Advantage, the expansion builds on more than 40 years of serving healthcare professionals. What began as a single Florida store in 1985 has grown into a national retail and e-commerce business, with a continued focus on helping healthcare workers find uniforms that fit their needs, their style, and their demanding workdays.

To find a store near you, including addresses and hours, visit uniformadvantage.com/stores.

About Uniform Advantage

Founded in 1985, Uniform Advantage is a leading retailer of medical uniforms, scrubs, footwear, and accessories. Through its retail stores and online shopping experience, the company offers healthcare professionals a wide selection of exclusive and national brands designed for comfort, performance, and personal style.

data.title: US judge approves Getty Images bankruptcy loan over shareholder objections
data.description:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - A US bankruptcy judge on Monday approved a $143 million bankruptcy loan for Getty Images ( GETYQ ) provided by Koch Equity Development, overruling objections from shareholders who had argued that the loan would allow Getty insiders to shortchange minority investors.

* US Bankruptcy Judge J. Kate Stickles in Delaware said the loan was the best available financing for Getty's bankruptcy restructuring

* Objecting shareholders had said the loan would essentially hand the company to the Getty family and Koch Equity Development while leaving other shareholders with nothing

* Stickles on Friday denied shareholders' request for a court-appointed committee to represent equity holders

* Getty cited court losses in investor litigation, its $1.46 billion ​in debt, a failed merger with Shutterstock, and increased competition from AI-generated imagery as reasons for its bankruptcy filing in October

* Getty said affiliates of ​the Getty family and Koch Equity Development, which committed to ​provide up to $533 million in new equity, will own 100% of the company after the bankruptcy restructuring

* Getty Images ( GETYQ ) expects to complete ​the restructuring by ​year-end

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: Update: US Equity Indexes Soar as Nvidia's Unexpected Move to Reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO Energizes AI Trade
data.description:
05:28 PM EST, 11/23/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Updates with index/price moves, macroeconomic data, and company news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes jumped after Nvidia's ( NVDA ) decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive officer injected life into the so-called AI trade, whistling past outrage from Democrats.

The Nasdaq Composite soared 5.6% to 24,089.56 on Monday's close, after trading close to bear-market territory at the end of last week. The S&P 500 catapulted 4.7% to 7,237.17, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 3% to 49,595.31. Both the S&P 500 and the Dow had fallen into correction territory on Friday.

All sectors except energy and consumer staples rose. Technology was up 9%, followed by communication services and consumer discretionary.

"The [US] government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia ( NVDA ) poses any risk to national security," US President Donald Trump said in a social media post. "The Attorney General of the [US] has confirmed that the US government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) shares shot up over 31%, the top performer on the S&P 500, the Nasdaq, and the Dow.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) success is driven less by its chips' performance and more by its "culture of innovation, ecosystem of incumbency, and massive investment in software, models, and services," according to a Truist Securities note. The culture of innovation was driven by Huang's "technical brilliance and magnetic personality," but the "downside/risks that remain are legal/regulatory," the note said.

Shares of CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ) soared more than 22% and 20%, respectively, among the biggest Nasdaq gainers, as Huang's return eases the circular-financing risk surrounding neocloud companies with relatively high levels of debt.

The VanEck Semiconductor Exchange Traded Fund, with about $66.44 billion in assets under management, blew past 15%, reflecting strength in the AI trade.

At its quarterly earnings call in November, Nvidia ( NVDA ) told analysts it does not plan to bring Huang back as CEO. That course of action, however, changed on Monday.

"The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia ( NVDA ), and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Chair Harvey Jones said in a statement on Monday. "The board received input from senior levels of the [US] government, and based on that input, the board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Huang, NVIDIA ( NVDA ) executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with US export controls," Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, said in a statement.

"The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement," Warren said. "Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA ( NVDA ) does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk."

In economic news, S&P Global's November flash reading of manufacturing conditions fell to a three-month low of 54.5 from 54.9 in October, as expected in a Bloomberg-compiled survey.

In energy markets, the front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract slumped 3.6% to $80.38 per barrel, while global benchmark Brent declined 3.4% to $89.46 per barrel.

In precious metals, gold futures jumped 3.3% to $3,631.4, and silver futures soared 4.5% to $42.90.

CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) shares slumped 8.9%, the worst performer on the SP 500 and the Nasdaq, after the company said Monday it has agreed to acquire Zscaler (ZS) in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion.

Arm (ARM) shares rose 16% after the company said CEO Rene Haas has agreed to remain in the role through 2033 under a new agreement.

Appetite for AI-linked shares returned after last week's steep selloff that pushed the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) was the top gainer on the S&P 500 and the Dow Monday, closing nearly 32% higher.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board reinstated Huang as chief executive Monday, saying US government officials assured that Huang doesn't pose national security risk.

Huang's return means Nvidia ( NVDA ) can continue to be "a strong proponent for the AI industry with access to the highest levels of government to voice opinions that should presumably benefit the entirety of the AI industry," Wedbush Securities said.

The decision to bring Huang back is a major catalyst for the chipmaking giant, but the reinstatement itself doesn't end scrutiny around governance and export controls, BofA Securities said Monday.

Technology stocks Dell (DELL), Micron Technology ( MU ) , Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) , Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ) , and Intel ( INTC ) all gained double-digit percentages.

In other corporate news, CrowdStrike's ( CRWD ) shares plunged 8.9%, the worst performer on the S&P 500. Zscaler ( ZS ) shares jumped 18%.

Treasury yields were higher, with the two-year rate increasing 6.6 basis points to 4.68% and the 10-year rate rising 2 basis points to 4.93%.

US private-sector growth decelerated to a four-month low in November amid softening demand, while price pressures showed signs of cooling, S&P Global's ( SPGI ) flash purchasing managers' index showed Monday.

S&P 500 third-quarter earnings growth accelerated on a weekly basis, buoyed by broad-based profit and revenue gains across all sectors, Oppenheimer Asset Management said in a report Monday. Another 13 S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report results this week.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil fell 4% to $80.06 a barrel in Monday late-afternoon trade, while Brent declined 3.7% to $89.18 a barrel.

Spot gold gained 2.8% to $3,637.30 per troy ounce, while silver jumped 4.5% to $43.41 per ounce.

data.title: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervention in abrupt board reversal
data.description:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - Nvidia ( NVDA ) reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO under pressure from US President Donald Trump, a stunning reversal following his resignation over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China.

Huang's comeback caps a whirlwind week of events that roiled markets and tore through the AI ecosystem that has relied on Nvidia ( NVDA ) for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.

But the board's about-face - less than a week after Chairman Harvey Jones said Nvidia ( NVDA ) would not rehire Huang as CEO because his personal behavior was inconsistent with the company's code of conduct - raises questions about its independence, governance experts said, even as the company's investigation remains unfinished.

Huang's comeback boosted Wall Street and sent Nvidia's ( NVDA ) shares soaring 33%, on track to add more than $900 billion in market value. The gains, however, were not enough to erase all losses since his resignation on November 12.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) said in a statement that based on US government input the board was confident that "Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk," a claim backed by Trump in an interview with CNBC.

Huang said in a statement that he was honored to return and "can't wait to get back to work." He returned to company headquarters to cheers from employees and said he was going to "be a better CEO the second time around," Business Insider reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.

"Jensen's return is not a total shock, but it does send a troubling message about the state of corporate governance in America," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer at Ocean Park Asset Management. "Certain executives are going to be held to different standards if you are perceived to be a one of one," he said, adding Huang would still have to answer "some tough questions from Congress."

Lawmakers across party lines strongly objected to Huang's reinstatement.

US Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Trump was "putting his own financial interests ... before our national security," while Senator Pete Ricketts, a Nebraska Republican, said Huang's return "doesn't absolve Nvidia ( NVDA ) of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips."

TRUMP'S SUPPORT FOR HUANG

Huang returned at the strong urging of Trump, industry leaders including Elon Musk, and some investors. His departure had reverberated from Silicon Valley to Taipei. A petition calling for his reinstatement drew more than 180,000 signatures, underscoring the unusually strong support for an executive who stepped down amid controversy.

"I believe my intervention was very important to get Jensen Huang back," Trump told CNBC.

The board did not mention Huang's affairs. Apart from Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman who is accused of having ties with Beijing, Huang is accused of having had intimate relationships with at least two Nvidia ( NVDA ) employees.

Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologized, but has not publicly addressed the individual alleged relationships in detail. China has denied the espionage allegations. Attempts by Reuters to reach Alice Huang have been unsuccessful.

Huang's return echoes OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's return as CEO four days after his ouster in 2023, after employees threatened to leave unless he was reinstated. Other founders and former bosses have returned in a crisis, from Steve Jobs at Apple to Bob Iger at Disney, but comebacks after personal misconduct are rare.

"There were definitely a lot of people who wanted him back. The extent that the administration intervened, the extent that shareholders intervened, it will be impossible to know," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers.

"But it tells us to some extent that Jensen Huang was too big to be fired."

CHINA IS KEY TO NVIDIA

The moves come as Nvidia ( NVDA ) faces heightened scrutiny in Washington over the flow of advanced AI chips to China. US authorities have tightened licensing rules for some chip shipments and overseas data centers serving Chinese companies, while lawmakers are preparing to question Huang, who has pushed for greater access to the Chinese market.

Trump told CNBC that he had urged Nvidia ( NVDA ) to continue reviewing its compliance with US export controls to ensure it was adequately protecting national security. Trump, who visited Shenzhen last week, told CNBC he had spoken to Chinese President Xi Jinping about Huang.

Huang's exit from Nvidia ( NVDA ) threatened its business in China, Reuters reported on Monday, with some customers there cancelling or hesitating to place orders, jeopardizing billions in revenue.

The Nvidia ( NVDA ) board has formed a committee to investigate whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted Huang and is also starting a search to name a new chief compliance officer. The company said CFO Colette Kress would continue as CFO.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) last week also created a committee focused on national security and export controls, while raising its annual sales-growth target and forecasting fourth-quarter revenue above Wall Street estimates.

LEGAL OVERHANG

Huang has agreed to testify before the US Senate in a public hearing on December 3, the Senate Banking Committee said. Huang's personal spokesperson declined to comment.

The company is also facing multiple investigations over issues ranging from potential accounting irregularities to suspected chip smuggling, and a shareholder lawsuit accusing the company and Huang of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.

Securities fraud plaintiffs must show that Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Huang knowingly misled investors, that investors relied on those misleading statements and that those misleading statements artificially inflated the stock.

Reuters reported exclusively last week that Huang misled several of the company's leaders, including its general counsel, Tim Teter, about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang. Teter did not respond to a request for comment and representatives for Huang and an Nvidia ( NVDA ) spokesperson declined to comment.

(Reporting by Anhata Rooprai and Deborah Sophia in Bengaluru and David Morgan in Washington; Additional reporting Saqib Ahmed and Chibuike Oguh; Writing by Sayantani Ghosh; Editing by Anil D'Silva, Saumyadeb Chakrabarty and Matthew Lewis)

data.title: Tuya Reports Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results and Declaration of Cash Dividend
data.description:
SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tuya Inc. ( TUYA ) , a global leading AI cloud platform service provider, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and the declaration of a cash dividend.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Total revenue was US$98.6 million, up approximately 19.5% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$82.5 million).

  • Platform-as-a-service ("PaaS") revenue was US$70.1 million, up approximately 18.3% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$59.2 million).

  • AI application & others revenue was US$13.6 million, up approximately 18.6% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$11.5 million).

  • Smart home & robot product revenue was US$15.0 million, up approximately 26.7% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$11.8 million).

  • Overall gross margin was 45.8%, down 2.5 percentage points year-over-year (3Q2025: 48.3%). Gross margin of PaaS was 45.7% (3Q2025: 48.8%).

  • Operating margin was 9.0%, up 4.4 percentage points year-over-year (3Q2025: 4.6%). Non-GAAP operating margin was 9.5% (3Q2025: 10.8%).

  • Net margin was 18.8%, improved by 0.6 percentage points year-over-year (3Q2025: 18.2%). Non-GAAP net margin was 19.3% (3Q2025: 24.4%).

  • Net profit was US$18.5 million (3Q2025: US$15.0 million). Non-GAAP net profit was US$19.1 million (3Q2025: US$20.1 million).

  • Net cash generated from operating activities was US$12.7 million (3Q2025: US$30.0 million).

  • Total cash and cash equivalents, time deposits and treasury securities recorded as short-term and long-term investments were US$971.9 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to US$1,017.3 million as of December 31, 2025.

For further information on the non-GAAP financial measures presented above, see the section headed "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

Third Quarter 2026 Operating Highlights

  • Premium PaaS customers[1] for the trailing 12 months ended September 30, 2026 were 331 (3Q2025: 280). In the third quarter of 2026, the Company's premium PaaS customers contributed approximately 89.6% of its PaaS revenue (3Q2025: approximately 88.0%).

  • Registered AI developers were over 2,180,000 as of September 30, 2026, up approximately 21.0% from approximately 1,801,000 developers as of December 31, 2025.
  1. The Company defines a premium PaaS customer as a customer as of a given date that contributed more than US$100,000 of PaaS revenue during the immediately preceding 12-month period.

Mr. Xueji (Jerry) Wang, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Tuya ( TUYA ), commented, "In the third quarter, opportunities and challenges coexisted in the global consumer electronics industry. On the one hand, AI-native hardware continued to move from concept toward deployment at scale. New categories such as companion robots and AI toys rose rapidly, becoming a new engine for industry growth, which fully demonstrated that users' new demands for hardware in the AI era have begun to emerge. On the other hand, upstream component costs such as memory chips were still rising, and demand in traditional categories also faced pressure. Against this backdrop, we still maintained solid growth, with total revenue increasing by 19.5% year over year to US$98.6 million. The growth rate further accelerated compared to the second quarter, and we achieved year-over-year growth for the 13th consecutive quarter. In particular, PaaS revenue grew by 18.3% year over year, reflecting the continued increase in penetration of smart products across different regions and categories.

We continued to fully embrace AI and accelerated the promotion of ecosystem deployment. During the quarter, shipments of new AI-native categories grew by over 400% year over year. We debuted the AI home companion robot Doova at IFA in Berlin and the Global Digital Trade Expo. With the AI life assistant Hey Tuya as a core entry point, we integrated the three major application ecosystems of AI Home, AI Robot, and AI Energy, as well as the full-stack Matter combo solution. At the same time, subscription businesses such as door lock value-added services and pet cloud storage developed steadily, driving a continuous increase in the proportion of recurring revenue. Regarding developer tools, following Tuya Cobuilder, we launched the AI-native no-code application development platform Tuya AI Coding this quarter, extending developer tools from hardware development to application development. Looking ahead, we will focus on the three major scenarios mentioned above to promote large-scale shipments and the commercialization of AI-native hardware such as companion robots, pet care devices, and home energy management devices, and continue to improve the developer toolchain, Agent orchestration, and commercialization capabilities."

Mr. Yi (Alex) Yang, Director and Chief Financial Officer of Tuya ( TUYA ), added, "In the third quarter, all three business segments delivered year-over-year revenue growth, with total revenue increasing by 19.5% year over year to US$98.6 million. As a foundation for our growth, the PaaS business saw its revenue increase by 18.3% year over year to US$70.1 million; Premium PaaS customers contributed approximately 89.6% of the PaaS revenue, and the core customer base remained stable. Smart home & robot product revenue grew by 26.7% year over year to US$15.0 million, primarily benefiting from growth in demand for categories such as AI audio and video, AI companion toys, and energy. AI application & others revenue increased by 18.6% year over year to US$13.6 million, primarily driven by the growth in cloud services, AI video cloud storage, and AI value-added services."

Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

REVENUE

Total revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 19.5% to US$98.6 million from US$82.5 million in the same period of 2025.

  • PaaS revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 18.3% to US$70.1 million from US$59.2 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to increasing demand compared with the same period of 2025 and the Company's strategic focus on customer needs and product enhancements, despite the disruptions in the international business environment due to tariff-related headwinds since April 2025. Our core customer base remained stable.

  • AI application & others revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 18.6% to US$13.6 million from US$11.5 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to an increase in revenue from cloud-based services. During the quarter, the Company remained committed to offering recurring value-added services with AI application functions.

  • Smart home & robot product revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 26.7% to US$15.0 million from US$11.8 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to growing customer demands.

GROSS PROFIT AND GROSS MARGIN

Total gross profit in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 13.6% to US$45.2 million from US$39.8 million in the same period of 2025. The gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 45.8%, compared to 48.3% in the same period of 2025.

  • PaaS gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 45.7%, compared to 48.8% in the same period of 2025, partly attributable to recent price fluctuations in the semiconductor supply chain.

  • AI application & others gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 75.7%, compared to 70.8% in the same period of 2025.

  • Smart home & robot product gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 19.3%, compared to 23.8% in the same period of 2025.

Gross margin fluctuated primarily due to changes in product and solution mix, as well as fluctuations in semiconductor supply-chain pricing. As an AI developer platform with a rich ecosystem of smart devices and applications, the Company remains focused on AI offering with compelling value propositions while maintaining economic efficiency.

OPERATING EXPENSES

Operating expenses increased by 0.8% to US$36.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 from US$36.0 million in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP operating expenses increased by 15.9% to US$35.8 million in the third quarter of 2026 from US$30.9 million in the same period of 2025. For further information on the non-GAAP financial measures presented above, see the section headed "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

  • Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$25.0 million, up 9.7% from US$22.8 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to i) higher employee-related cost and outsourced labor cost of US$1.8 million, ii) higher third-party cloud service fees of US$0.4 million, iii) partially offset by lower share-based compensation expenses of US$0.8 million as equity incentive awards granted at higher valuations in previous years have been gradually amortized. Non-GAAP adjusted research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$24.6 million, compared to US$21.7 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Sales and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$9.3 million, up 16.9% from US$8.0 million in the same period of 2025, primarily because of i) higher employee-related cost of US$0.9 million, ii) higher third-party cloud expense of US$0.2 million, iii) partially offset by lower share-based compensation expenses of US$0.4 million as equity incentive awards granted at higher valuations in previous years have been gradually amortized. Non-GAAP adjusted sales and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$9.3 million, compared to US$7.5 million in the same period of 2025.

  • General and administrative expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$5.3 million, down 38.0% from US$8.5 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to i) lower share-based compensation expenses of US$3.4 million as equity incentive awards granted at higher valuations in previous years have been gradually amortized, ii) partially offset by higher employee-related cost of US$0.3 million. Non-GAAP adjusted general and administrative expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$5.1 million, compared to US$4.9 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Other operating incomes, net in the third quarter of 2026 was US$3.3 million, primarily due to the receipt of software value-added tax refunds.

PROFIT FROM OPERATIONS AND OPERATING MARGIN

Profit from operations in the third quarter of 2026 was US$8.9 million, compared to US$3.8 million in the same period of 2025. The Company had a non-GAAP profit from operations of US$9.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to US$8.9 million in the same period of 2025, demonstrating consistent operating profitability and leverage.

Operating margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 9.0%, up 4.4 percentage points from 4.6% in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP operating margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 9.5%, down 1.3 percentage points from 10.8% in the same period of 2025.

NET PROFIT AND NET MARGIN

Net profit in the third quarter of 2026 was US$18.5 million, an increase of 23.8% from US$15.0 million in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP net profit in the third quarter of 2026 was US$19.1 million, compared to US$20.1 million in the same period of 2025.

Net margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 18.8%, an improvement of 0.6 percentage points from 18.2% in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP net margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 19.3%, compared to 24.4% in the same period of 2025.

BASIC AND DILUTED NET PROFIT PER ADS

Basic and diluted net profit per ADS was US$0.03 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to US$0.02 in the same period of 2025. Each ADS represents one Class A ordinary share.

Non-GAAP basic and diluted net profit per ADS was US$0.03 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to US$0.03 in the same period of 2025.

CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS, TIME DEPOSITS AND TREASURY SECURITIES RECORDED AS SHORT-TERM AND LONG-TERM INVESTMENTS

Cash and cash equivalents, time deposits and treasury securities recorded as short-term and long-term investments were US$971.9 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to US$1,017.3 million as of December 31, 2025. The Company believes its current cash position is sufficient to meet its current liquidity and working capital needs.

NET CASH GENERATED FROM OPERATING ACTIVITIES

Net cash generated from operating activities in the third quarter of 2026 was US$12.7 million, compared to US$30.0 million in the same period of 2025. The net cash generated from operating activities for the third quarter of 2026 was mainly attributable to working capital changes in the ordinary course of business.

For further information on non-GAAP financial measures presented above, see the section headed "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

Business Outlook

Currently, innovative AI hardware is in a rapid ramp-up phase, but the overall macroeconomic environment remains complex. On the one hand, AI-native hardware is moving from concept toward deployment at scale, with new categories such as companion robots and AI toys rising rapidly, becoming a new engine for industry growth. On the other hand, upstream component costs such as memory chips continue to rise, demand recovery in certain traditional categories is relatively slow, and uncertainties relating to trade policies and supply chains remain. Performance varies across regions, categories and markets. With the accelerated integration of AI and consumer hardware, Physical AI scenarios are ushering in a broader space for development.

Against this backdrop, we will continue to advance our AI-driven strategy. At the product level, we will focus on three high-potential scenarios, namely AI Home, AI Energy and AI Robot, to promote large-scale shipments and the commercialization of AI-native hardware such as companion robots, home energy management devices, and pet care devices. At the developer platform level, we will continue to improve Tuya Cobuilder, Tuya AI Coding and Agent orchestration capabilities, further lowering the development threshold, and enabling more customers and brands to quickly launch their own AI applications based on the Tuya ( TUYA ) platform. At the user application level, we will continue to enhance the response efficiency and reliability of Hey Tuya, and advance subscription and value-added services such as AI-powered protection, AI energy saving, pet care, and video understanding, to enhance our renewal and ongoing service capabilities.

Looking ahead, we will maintain disciplined execution, and continuously invest in AI R&D and platform capabilities. We will focus on AI-native applications, Physical AI scenarios, and developer platform construction, leveraging the advantages of our platform, device ecosystem and global developer base to transform AI technology from a tool capability into real and scalable commercial value. At the same time, we also recognize that our future performance may be affected by changes in consumer demand, regional economic conditions, inventory cycles, component and logistics costs, foreign exchange and interest-rate volatility, tariffs and trade-policy adjustments, and broader geopolitical uncertainties.

Declaration of Cash Dividend and Record Date

On November 23, 2026, the Board approved the declaration and distribution of a cash dividend (the "Cash Dividend") of US$0.0570 per ordinary share, or US$0.0570 per ADS, to such holders as at the close of business on January 6, 2027, Hong Kong Time and New York Time, respectively. data.title: TRADING DAY-Market euphoria as Huang returns to Nvidia
data.description:
ORLANDO, Florida, Nov 23 (Reuters) - US stocks roared back on Monday, as the stunning return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia ( NVDA ) triggered a sizzling rally in tech and AI companies - Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares rose more than 30%. The euphoria lifted the dollar to its highest level since March last year, but bonds were much more muted, with the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rising barely a single basis point.

In my column today, I argued that the imploding AI trade would not only throw doubt on the wisdom of Fed rate hikes, but could even put rate cuts back on the table. That scenario seems less likely now, at least in the near term, given the extraordinary events at Nvidia ( NVDA ). But if today has taught us anything, it is that you can't rule anything in or out these days.

Today's Key Reads

* Nvidia ( NVDA ) reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO amid pressure from Trump, investors

* Trump saw Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Huang as protector of open-weight AI models, sources say

* US lawmakers criticize Nvidia ( NVDA ) decision to reinstate Huang as CEO

* Oil's Iran war recovery masks a stubborn diesel shortage: Bousso

* CrowdStrike snaps up Zscaler in $44 billion deal as cyber threats mount

* Today's Key Market Moves * STOCKS: Japan -5%, South Korea -3%. Europe +2%, UK +1%. Nasdaq +6.5%, Dow +3%, S&P 500 +4.7%, breaking longest losing streak since April 2024. * SECTORS/SHARES: Nine sectors in the S&P 500 rise, two fall. Tech +9%, comms services +5%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) +31%, Dell +20%, Micron Technology +18%, "neoclouds" CoreWeave ( CRWV ) +22%, Nebius +20%. Anthropic -1.4%, CrowdStrike -9%. * FX: Dollar +0.5% to strongest since March last year. Brazilian real falls through 6.00/$, now down 17% since presidential election runoff one month ago. * BONDS: US yields +7 bps at the short end, bear flattening the curve. US 2-year auction draws strong demand from direct bidders, soft demand from indirects, according to Vanda Macro Intelligence. * COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil slumps 3-4% to three-month low. Gold +3% to $3,640/oz.

Today's Talking Points:

Jensen burner

Where to begin? Monday, November 23, 2026, will go down as one of the most extraordinary days in US market history. Only 11 days after resigning as CEO of chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ) under a cloud of scandal, Jensen Huang returned to run the company he co-founded 33 years ago. This astonishing reversal came after a 23% plunge in Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares last week meant the firm had lost half of its value - around $2.8 trillion - since shares peaked on October 6. It also followed direct, personal intervention from President Donald Trump.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) 31% surge on Monday helped lift the Nasdaq by 6%, the S&P 500 by 5%, and the chip index by 12%. Relief rallies don't come much bigger than this. But once the dust settles on Monday's session, major questions around Huang and Nvidia ( NVDA ) remain. Both are still the subject of various investigations, and despite Trump's assurances, US lawmakers are almost certain to seek answers on potential national security breaches. This drama will run for some time, and given the turn of events on Monday, it is impossible to say how it unfolds.

Hello, good buy

The dollar on Monday hit its highest level against a basket of major currencies since March last year, propelled by the sizzling "risk-on" stock market rally as Wall Street cheered the return of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Huang. Its 0.5% rise was solid. Nothing remarkable here, except that the dollar was also surging to similar peaks on "safe haven" demand after Huang resigned earlier this month.

It seems like the dollar is in a sweet spot - it's in demand when market volatility forces investors to sell risky assets to raise liquidity, and when foreign investors want in on booming stock prices. If this equity rebound continues, the dollar will probably also draw support from renewed hawkishness around the Fed outlook. In the short term, at least, it's a win-win-win. Almost too good to be true.

Jensen and hedges

Stock markets' initial euphoria over Huang's return to Nvidia ( NVDA ) on Monday will have drawn huge sighs of relief from many investors around the world. And regulators. The gloomy end to last week prompted authorities in China, Taiwan and South Korea to take steps over the weekend and early on Monday to prop up sliding markets. They included tightening rules around short selling, easing requirements for margin financing, and readying the immediate release of emergency stabilisation funds.

The huge rebound on Wall Street on Monday and expected bounce in Asia on Tuesday put these measures on the back burner. But it's a reminder of how fragile sentiment had gotten, and how vulnerable these markets - and economies - are to the AI unwind. There's no room for complacency.

What could move markets tomorrow?

* Japan PMIs (November, flash estimate)

* Germany Ifo business index (November)

* US Treasury sells $70 billion of 5-year notes at auction

* Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem speaks

* The latest twists and turns in the Nvidia ( NVDA ) drama

data.title: US blacklists Megaspeed chip firm linked to Nvidia scandal
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The United States on Monday added Singapore-based chip firm Megaspeed, which is closely tied to an espionage investigation involving Nvidia ( NVDA ), to its trade blacklist.

The addition of the company follows revelations that Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and Megaspeed's controlling shareholder who is reportedly alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

The move coincided with Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia ( NVDA ) after his resignation two weeks ago over revelations of extramarital affairs.

US companies cannot ship goods, software and technology to companies on ​the entity list without a license, which is likely to be denied. Firms on the list can find it harder to get access to US-origin spare parts, software updates or licenses for intellectual property.

Megaspeed did not immediately return a request for comment.

The New York Times reported last month that US authorities had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset who passed information to Beijing while developing a close relationship with the Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO.

Reuters could not independently verify the intelligence allegation. China has said the spy accusations are "groundless."

Alice Huang led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia ( NVDA ) chip customer, people familiar with the matter have said. US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the US Justice and Commerce departments said this week.

Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducted "lawful business." Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) lists Megaspeed as an official cloud partner in its directory. Megaspeed attracted public attention in October 2025, when the New York Times reported it was under US investigation over whether it was helping Chinese customers obtain advanced Nvidia ( NVDA ) chips subject to Washington's export controls.

The last time the Commerce Department placed any new entities on the list was October 2025.

As Reuters exclusively reported in June, the US has held off adding China's AI startup DeepSeek, memory chipmaker CXMT and more than 100 other companies flagged as national security risks to the trade blacklist, as the Trump administration tried to avoid escalating tensions with Beijing.

(Reporting by Chris Sanders and Karen Freifeld; Editing by Tom Hogue and Alistair Bell)

data.title: Fed has 'work to do' to lower inflation, Williams says
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 23 (Reuters) - New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point the US central bank toward tighter monetary policy.

"We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis," Williams said in remarks prepared for delivery to an event at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York City. "There is still work to do to get that done." 

Williams said inflation is "too high" and that it must be lowered back to the Fed's target "in a timely manner and on a sustained basis." He noted that he will continue to assess incoming data to decide what action the central bank should take at its December 8-9 policy meeting.

Financial markets broadly expect the Fed to raise its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point next month from the current 3.75%-4.00% range, with more increases to come next year.

The Fed last raised rates in September as part of an effort to curb inflation, which has been above the 2% target for more than five years. Central bank officials worry that, if this situation persists, the public could lose confidence that inflation will return to that level.

Williams was speaking the same day as a sharp stock market rally, triggered by chipmaker Nvidia's announcement that it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, after President Donald Trump urged it to do so. Investors' reaction highlighted the importance of AI companies in driving the markets. Some observers had wondered in recent days whether sharp stock losses might deter the Fed from raising rates.

In his remarks, Williams said that he expects inflation to end the year at 3.5% and to moderate to just above 2% next year before easing to the target in 2028. He also noted that risks to inflation continue to be skewed to the upside.

Williams noted that among the key drivers of high price pressures, energy prices remain elevated and the outlook on that front is uncertain.

He added that "although the effects of tariffs, geopolitical conflicts, and the AI surge are showing up in prices of certain categories of goods, there is little evidence of these spilling over significantly into broader and more persistent inflation."

Williams also said the economy is showing strength and resilience and should grow by 2.75% in both 2026 and 2027. He added that the job market has been showing stability, and the current 4.1% unemployment rate should fall to around 4% next year.

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: CANADA STOCKS-TSX posts biggest daily gain since April 2025, led by tech and mining
data.description:
(Updates at market close)

By Fergal Smith

TORONTO, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Canada's main stock index rose by the most in 19 months on Monday as a rebound in gold prices boosted mining shares and after Nvidia ( NVDA ) reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, reviving optimism for the AI trade.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended up 891.59 points, or 2.69%, at 34,081.44, which snapped a sequence of seven straight daily declines and marked the index's biggest daily gain since April 2025.

* The TSX was bouncing back after it posted on Friday its lowest closing level in seven months. Friday's decline had left the index down more than 10% from its record closing high on August 25, confirming a correction

* Wall Street's main indexes also rallied sharply as a rebound in Nvidia's ( NVDA ) shares helped lift sentiment across chipmakers after weeks of heavy selling

* "Corrections are uncomfortable, and they are normal," Philip Petursson and Pierre-Benoît Gauthier, investment strategists at IG Wealth Management, said in a note

* "And while we may not have reached bottom yet, there are enough indicators that we follow to suggest this correction is creating opportunities for long-term investors," the strategists said

* The technology sector rose 4.4%, with shares of Celestica ( CLS ), which provides hardware solutions for data centers, up 6.4%

* The materials sector, which includes metal mining shares, jumped 6.4%

* Gold prices recovered from a more than one-year low as investors bought the dip, while the market looked ahead to upcoming US inflation data for further clues on the Federal Reserve's interest rate trajectory

* Financials, the most heavily weighted sector on the TSX, rose 2.7% and industrials ended 2.2% higher

* Energy was the only major sector to lose ground, falling 1.5%

* US crude oil futures settled 3.9% lower at $80.17 a barrel as traders weighed a rise in supplies from the Middle East and the restart of a Libyan oil pipeline

(Reporting by Fergal Smith in Toronto and Utkarsh Hathi in Bengaluru; Editing by Shreya Biswas and Diane Craft)

Guangzhou, China, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Youxin Technology Ltd ( YAAS ) (“Youxin Technology” or the “Company”), a software as a service (“SaaS”) and platform as a service (“PaaS”) provider committed to helping retail enterprises digitally transform their businesses, today announced that, at the Company’s annual general meeting, the Company’s shareholders have approved, by ordinary resolution, authorizing the Company’s board of directors to conduct a share consolidation of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares at a ratio of one-for-six, with an expected market effective date of November 27, 2026. The objective of the share consolidation is to increase the per-share trading price of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares and provide the Company with greater flexibility to support the continued listing and marketability of its securities.

Beginning with the opening of trading on November 27, 2026, the Company’s Class A ordinary shares will trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market on a split-adjusted basis, under the same symbol “YAAS” but under a new CUSIP number, G9876W146.

The share consolidation will reduce the number of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares issued and outstanding from approximately 6,769,352 to approximately 1,128,226 (subject to adjustment due to the effect of rounding up fractional shares into whole shares). The authorized number of Class A ordinary shares will be reduced by the same ratio, from 163,800,000,000 to 27,300,000,000, and the par value of each Class A ordinary share will increase from US$0.04 to US$0.24. The Company’s Class B ordinary shares are not being consolidated and are not affected by the share consolidation. The number of Class A ordinary shares issuable upon exercise of the Company’s outstanding warrants and equity awards, and the applicable exercise prices, will be proportionately adjusted in accordance with their respective terms.

As a result of the share consolidation, each six pre-split ordinary shares outstanding will automatically combine and convert to one issued and outstanding Class A ordinary share without any action on the part of the shareholder. Discussion of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

This press release includes non-GAAP financial measures derived from the company's Consolidated Statements of Operations. These measures are not presented in accordance with, nor are they a substitute for U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, or GAAP. These measures include: non-GAAP gross profit; non-GAAP gross margin; non-GAAP operating expense; non-GAAP operating earnings; non-GAAP operating earnings margin; non-GAAP earnings before taxes; non-GAAP net earnings; non-GAAP net earnings per diluted share, non-GAAP dilutive shares; and non-GAAP EBITDA. The company is providing a reconciliation above of each non-GAAP financial measure used in this earnings release to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.

The company utilizes a number of different financial measures, both GAAP and non-GAAP, in analyzing and assessing the overall performance of its business, in making operating decisions, and forecasting and planning for future periods. The company considers the use of the non-GAAP measures to be helpful in assessing the performance of the ongoing operation of its business by excluding unusual and one-time costs. The company believes that disclosing non-GAAP financial measures provides useful supplemental data that allows for greater transparency in the review of its financial and operational performance. The company also believes that disclosing non-GAAP financial measures provides useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating its operating results and future prospects in the same manner as management and in comparing financial results across accounting periods and to those of peer companies.

Non-GAAP measures include the following items:

Amortization of intangible assets: The company does not acquire businesses and assets on a predictable cycle. The amount of purchase price allocated to intangible assets and the term of amortization can vary significantly and are unique to each acquisition or asset purchase. The company believes that excluding amortization of intangible assets allows the users of its financial statements to better review and understand the historic and current results of its operations, and also facilitates comparisons to peer companies.

Purchase price accounting charges to cost of revenues: The company may incur charges to cost of revenues as a result of acquisitions. The company believes that excluding these charges allows the users of its financial statements to better understand the historic and current cost of its products, its gross margin, and also facilitates comparisons to peer companies.

Restructuring charges: The company incurs restructuring charges that result from events which arise from unforeseen circumstances and/or often occur outside of the ordinary course of its on-going business. Although these events are reflected in its GAAP financials, these unique transactions may limit the comparability of its on-going operations with prior and future periods.

Acquisition and integration related costs: The company incurs expenses or benefits with respect to certain items associated with its acquisitions, such as transaction costs, changes in fair value of acquisition related hedges, changes in the fair value of contingent consideration liabilities, gain or expense on settlement of pre-existing relationships, etc. The company excludes such expenses or benefits as they are related to acquisitions and have no direct correlation to the operation of its on-going business. The company also incurs expenses or benefits with respect to certain items associated with its acquisitions, such as integration costs relating to acquisition costs incurred prior to closing and up to 12 months after the closing date of the acquisition.

Impairment charges: The company may incur impairment charges that result from events which arise from unforeseen circumstances and/or often occur outside of the ordinary course of its on-going business and such charges may limit the comparability of its on-going operations with prior and future periods.

Non-ordinary course litigation: The company may incur charges that result from non-ordinary course litigation matters such as certain intellectual property disputes and joint venture litigation. Litigation matters that are part of the ordinary course of the company’s business, such as product liability claims, employment related matters and commercial contract disputes, are not excluded.

Other non-operational costs: Certain items may be non-recurring, unusual, infrequent and directly related to an event that is distinct and non-reflective of the company’s ongoing business operations. These may include such items as legal settlements, inventory write-downs for discontinued products, cost of facilities no longer in use, extinguishment of debt and hedge costs, environmental settlements, governmental settlements including tax settlements, and other items of similar nature.

Non-operational tax adjustments: Certain tax items may be non-recurring, unusual, infrequent and directly related to an event that is distinct and non-reflective of the company’s normal business operations. These may include such items as the retroactive impact of significant changes in tax laws, including changes to statutory tax rates and one-time tax charges.

Tax effects of operating earnings adjustments: The company applies its non-GAAP adjustments to the GAAP pretax income to calculate the non-GAAP effective tax rate. This application of its non-GAAP effective tax rate excludes any discrete items, as defined in the guidance for accounting for income taxes in interim periods, or any other non-operational tax adjustments.

Gains and losses on equity-method investments: The company's net income (loss) is impacted by gains and losses associated with its equity-method investments in privately-held companies included in Other (expense) income, net on the Consolidated Statements of Operations. These gains and losses may arise from unforeseen circumstances and/or often occur outside of the ordinary course of the company's on-going business. By excluding these gains and losses, investors can better evaluate its operating performance period-over-period.

1 Other non-operational costs consist primarily of costs related to the early extinguishment of debt. For the twelve months ended October 2, 2026 and October 3, 2025 these costs totaled $9.4 million and $0.1 million, respectively. These amounts reflect losses incurred in connection with the early repayment, refinancing, or modification of existing debt agreements. Such costs are episodic, arise from discrete financing decisions, and are not reflective of the Company’s ongoing operating performance. Management believes excluding these amounts from its non‑GAAP results enhances comparability across periods and with peer companies and provides investors with a clearer view of the Company’s core operating results.

By Heather Schlitz

CHICAGO, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Chicago soybean futures rose on Monday, supported by strong demand for soymeal. Wheat and corn were choppy amid light volume in pre-Thanksgiving trading.

Chicago Board of Trade most-active soybeans settled 8 cents higher to $12.28-3/4 per bushel. Wheat ended 3-1/2 cents higher to $5.95-1/2 per bushel, and corn ended 1 cent higher to $4.49-3/4 per bushel.

"Holiday trade this week doesn't have the ingredients to give big moves in either direction with volume fading out as week goes on," said Randy Place, analyst at Hightower Report.

Soymeal has been firm amid improving demand, lending support to soybean futures.

"We're still trying to recover from tight meal supplies when the harvest started slow and we had crush plants that had to slow or shut down," Place said. "The meal pipeline has been slow to replenish over the last month or two."

Soybeans rose on Friday after the US Department of Agriculture announced sales of 100,000 metric tons of US soymeal to Spain.

Wheat gained underlying support from concerns about potential supply disruptions following a Baltic Sea shipping attack and new import demand with a big tender from Pakistan to buy 800,000 tons of wheat.

Hostilities between Russia and Ukraine were in focus, after a Russian cargo ship was hit by drones and caught fire in the Baltic Sea on Saturday, seen as an attack by Ukraine.

Russia has hugely expanded Baltic Sea exports since attacks stopped shipborne Black Sea exports in August, easing world supplies.

(Reporting by Heather Schlitz in Chicago. Additional reporting by Rajendra Jadhav in Mumbai and Michael Hogan; in Hamburg; Editing by Sonia Cheema, Diti Pujara and Diane Craft)

data.title: US agency to vote to ease ownership limits on local TV, radio stations
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The Federal Communications Commission plans to vote next month to ease ownership limits on local radio and TV stations as it vows to level the playing field for broadcasters with large tech companies.

FCC Chair Brendan Carr said the commission will vote on December 17 whether to lift the limits on the number of stations local broadcasters can own in the markets they operate in, replacing the limits with individual case-by-case reviews.

(Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Chris Reese)

data.title: Analysis-Huang's stunning Nvidia return sparks relief for battered AI trade
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 23 (Reuters) - For US stock investors, Monday's stunning return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang brought a sigh of relief for the battered AI trade, one worth trillions of dollars in market value.

Huang's reinstatement atop the semiconductor giant halted a severe slide in technology shares that had sent the benchmark S&P 500 into a correction amid growing doubts about the AI trade that had been the primary engine for the four-year-old bull stock market.

The reversal by Nvidia's board in bringing back Huang came after his abrupt departure earlier this month rattled an already anxious market. Concerns flared not only about Nvidia but also about the health of the AI ecosystem which the chip company has been at the center of. 

"You've basically had this perfect storm of uncertainty that has created a crisis of confidence," said King Lip, chief strategist at BakerAvenue Wealth Management in San Francisco. "This Nvidia fallout was one of those pieces of ...uncertainty. So this removes a pretty significant one with Jensen coming back."

Shares of Nvidia soared on news of Huang's return to the company he co-founded, rising 32% in early afternoon trading, equivalent to more than $900 billion in market capitalization added back to the value of the semiconductor company, whose stock price has been hammered in recent weeks.

Shares of companies across the AI industry rallied sharply, with the Nasdaq 100 that is concentrated in megacap tech companies jumping more than 6%.

"The initial reaction here is a big collective sigh of relief," said Thomas Urano, co-chief investment officer at Sage Advisory in Austin, Texas. "Maybe Jensen...puts confidence back in the AI trade."

Many investors had worried about the extent to which Nvidia's massive value was tied up in Huang, who was credited for foreseeing the technology shift that led to Nvidia's advanced chips that are central to the AI boom and to Nvidia's soaring profits.

Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress had been running the company on an interim basis while the company searched for a permanent replacement. 

"To try to replace Jensen was something that nobody could feel comfortable that they are going to find somebody to automatically fill his shoes," said Tom Plumb, portfolio manager of the Plumb Balanced Fund in Madison, Wisconsin. "But to have the visionary who was able to attract some of the most talented people in the industry ... it's certainly very, very positive for the company."

Huang has been "essentially the product manager of his company," said Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners. "And that's really important, which is why a lot of investors are happy to see him back."

More broadly, Nvidia has been tied to an array of companies involved in the sprawling AI buildout. Many investors had voiced concerns about the future of that ecosystem without Huang himself, who is seen as one of the most pivotal AI figures.

Some investors also said Huang's return could clear some regulatory clouds over the stock. Huang's resignation followed revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China. 

President Donald Trump, who said he secured the deal to bring back Huang, said in a post on Truth Social the US government had no reason to believe Huang's return posed a national security risk and had no evidence he had engaged in unlawful conduct.

Trump told CNBC that the stock market reaction to Huang's resignation from Nvidia "probably" factored into his decision to push for the CEO's reinstatement although his view of the long-term benefit of having Huang at the helm of the company was the bigger weight. 

Some regulatory clouds could remain. California's attorney general's office said on Monday that Huang's reinstatement does not diminish the need for a probe into what Nvidia told investors about its China ties.

And questions about the AI trade that had dogged the market before the Nvidia crisis erupted were likely to persist.

Those questions center around the sustainability of massive AI spending on data centers and other infrastructure, which has driven up profits for a broad swath of companies.

Concerns have grown about financing of those investments and whether they will generate sufficient returns. Meanwhile, a sweeping Democratic victory in the midterm elections earlier this month is driving expectations of stronger political pushback against the development of data centers in the US.

"We very well may see more selling pressure after this relief rally runs its course," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer at Ocean Park Asset Management in Santa Monica, California. "Jensen's return doesn't answer the big questions investors were grappling with."

(Reporting by Lewis Krauskopf, Chibuike Oguh and Chuck Mikolajczak, additional reporting by Anand Gopal; Editing by Megan Davies and Alistair Bell)

data.title: Abits Group Signs Letter of Intent to Acquire Soter Technologies, Advancing AI-Enabled Data Center Monitoring Strategy
data.description:
DUFF, TN / ACCESS Newswire / November 23, 2026 / Abits Group Inc ( ABTS ) ("Abits" or the "Company"), a U.S.-focused digital infrastructure company, today announced that it has signed a nonbinding letter of intent to acquire Soter Technologies, Inc. ("Soter"), a provider of environmental sensing technology and AI-enabled monitoring software. The proposed acquisition would support Abits' ( ABTS ) strategy to develop integrated digital infrastructure capabilities by adding technology that management believes could help data center operators predict and identify early warning signs of potential equipment and infrastructure problems, reducing unplanned downtime and improving operational reliability.

Stephen Faucetta, Chairman and CEO of Abits Group ( ABTS ), commented:

"Reliable operations are essential to data centers, particularly as increasing computing demands place greater pressure on uptime and availability. We believe Soter's combination of advanced sensors and AI-enabled monitoring software could provide operators with additional insight into environmental changes that may indicate, even predict, developing problems before they lead to equipment failures or service interruptions.

"Our strategy is to build a digital infrastructure platform that combines the facilities, power and technology needed to support increasingly demanding computing applications. We believe Soter's technology could complement our existing infrastructure, and we intend to evaluate how its sensing and monitoring capabilities can be adapted for AI and high-performance computing environments."

Enhancing Environmental Intelligence for Data Centers

Modern data centers employ sophisticated monitoring and management systems, including technologies designed to identify potential equipment problems before failures occur. Abits ( ABTS ) believes Soter's technology could complement these systems by providing an additional layer of environmental intelligence through its combination of sensors, acoustic monitoring and AI-enabled software.

Soter's FlySense platform incorporates sensors that monitor changes in air quality, airborne particles, sound patterns and other environmental conditions. Its cloud-based monitoring software analyzes sensor data and delivers automated alerts when unusual conditions are detected.

Abits ( ABTS ) and Soter believe these capabilities could be adapted to detect certain irregularities in data center environments. For example, changes in airborne particles associated with electrical equipment or unusual acoustic patterns from cooling fans and other mechanical systems may provide early indications of developing problems. Detecting these conditions could help facility operators investigate and address potential issues before they escalate into equipment damage or operational interruptions.

Abits ( ABTS ) and Soter will work together developing applications of its technology for data center infrastructure monitoring. These capabilities remain subject to further development, technical validation and integration with existing facility management systems.

Soter's FlySense sensors are manufactured in the United States, providing an established domestic manufacturing arrangement alongside Soter's software and monitoring capabilities.

If the acquisition is completed, Abits ( ABTS ) intends to evaluate deploying Soter's technology at its existing facilities and incorporating its capabilities into future AI and high-performance computing infrastructure projects.

Independent Growth Opportunities

Beyond its potential applications in data centers, Soter represents an established technology business with existing customers, recurring software revenue and opportunities to expand into additional markets.

Headquartered in Ronkonkoma, New York, Soter develops and markets its FlySense environmental sensing platform and cloud-based monitoring software. The company has worked with more than 3,000 school districts, and its technology is used in institutional and commercial environments to monitor air quality, vaping, unusual sound patterns and device tampering. Its platform provides continuous monitoring, reporting and automated alerts, allowing customers to oversee multiple facilities and respond to identified conditions.

Soter reports more than 30,000 active FlySense devices and generates revenue through hardware sales and paid monitoring and software subscriptions. The company currently has approximately 3,000 paying customers subscribing to its monitoring and software services, providing a recurring revenue stream. According to Soter management, the company is generating positive EBITDA, although its financial results remain subject to verification through Abits' ( ABTS ) due diligence.

If the acquisition is completed, Abits ( ABTS ) intends to operate Soter as a standalone business serving third-party customers while supporting the expansion of its existing product portfolio, recurring software services and customer base. The Company also sees opportunities to extend Soter's sensing and monitoring capabilities into additional markets, including manufacturing, industrial facilities, utilities and other environments where equipment reliability and continuous operations are important.

Abits ( ABTS ) intends to retain Soter's existing senior management team, subject to mutually acceptable agreements, and support the continued development and commercialization of its technology.

Proposed Acquisition

The letter of intent is nonbinding except for specified provisions. The proposed transaction remains subject to satisfactory due diligence, negotiation and execution of definitive agreements, required financing and approvals and other closing conditions. There can be no assurance that definitive agreements will be executed, that the acquisition will be completed or that the anticipated operating and strategic benefits will be realized.

About Abits Group Inc ( ABTS )

Abits Group Inc ( ABTS ) is a digital infrastructure company with operations in the United States. Through its U.S. subsidiary, Abit USA, Inc., the Company owns or operates infrastructure supporting energy-intensive computing applications. Abits ( ABTS ) is evaluating opportunities to expand its business into artificial intelligence, high-performance computing and related digital infrastructure services. Additional information is available at www.abitsgroup.com.

data.title: US STOCKS-Wall Street roars back, Nvidia jumps 31%  as Jensen Huang returns as CEO
data.description:
(Updates to afternoon)

* Nvidia ( NVDA ) reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, shares surge

* Nasdaq, S&P 500 head for biggest daily pct gain since April 2025

* Indexes up: Dow 3.3%, S&P 500 4.9%, Nasdaq 6.7%

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Ragini Mathur

Nov 23 (Reuters) - US stocks surged on Monday, led by a more than 6% jump in the Nasdaq as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO drove investors back into AI-related shares after last week's rout.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares shot up 31%, on track for their biggest daily percentage gain in more than two decades after the board reinstated Huang. The CEO resigned this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

US President Donald Trump said he secured a deal with Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board to bring back Huang as CEO. Nvidia ( NVDA ) is widely seen as a cornerstone of the AI trade.

The news helped Wall Street recover from a sharp selloff last week. The S&P 500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections on Friday as worries mounted about the AI trade.

The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion in market value on Monday, while the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 were set for their biggest daily gains since the market surged after Trump paused his "Liberation Day" tariff package in April 2025.

"The thought had been, and it's being borne out today, that Jensen Huang is uniquely important to Nvidia ( NVDA ) and to the AI trade," said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments.

But, he said, "you have one issue that is resolved -- and it's a biggie -- but you still have to see how the rest of things play out."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,568.61 points, or 3.26%, to 49,715.94, the S&P 500 rose 340.51 points, or 4.92%, to 7,250.38 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1,505.02 points, or 6.65%, to 24,122.76.

The Nasdaq had come close to entering a bear market as investors worried about the heavy borrowing underpinning AI investment and questioned whether the sector could deliver sufficient returns. Fears of political scrutiny also mounted after Democrats swept the US midterm elections.

Then on Monday, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was up 13% and on track for its biggest daily gain since April 2025. The S&P 500 information technology sector jumped 9.1% and led the gains in the benchmark index.

Among other megacap stocks, Amazon ( AMZN ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) , Meta and Alphabet were all sharply higher.

Also climbing were neocloud and data-center companies, which had come under sharp selling pressure following Huang's abrupt exit. CoreWeave ( CRWV ) rose 20.2%. Other sectors also rose, with energy being the only group in negative territory.

"Huang's return marks one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive," said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation.

"Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn't like what it saw."

Investors will now focus on Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report, which could give clues about the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook.

On the Nasdaq, 3,978 stocks rose and 1,006 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by about a 3.95-to-1 ratio. There were 68 new highs and 352 new lows.

On the NYSE, advancing issues outnumbered declining ones by a 4.8-to-1 ratio. There were 25 new highs and 200 new lows.

(Reporting by Caroline Valetkevitch in New York and Ragini Mathur in Bengaluru; additional reporting by Niket Nishant, Purvi Agarwal and Avinash P in Bengaluru; Editing by Rashmi Aich, Maju Samuel and David Gregorio)
